title: The one who would not bow

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? have you ever felt a flash of “i’m better than that”?
options: thank you for saying so. most people have. listen.
then this story will feel familiar.
lucky you. watch for it after this.

steps.line: God told the angels to bow before Adam, the first human. And they bowed, every one of them.

steps.q: Every one bowed, except Iblis. What reason do you think he gave?
steps.why: In the Qur’an his reason is a comparison: “I am better than him” (7:12). A few later Sufi writers imagined the other line for him, but it isn’t the Qur’an’s.

steps.line: All except Iblis. Elsewhere the Qur’an says he was of the jinn, beings made of fire. “What kept you from bowing?” God asked.
“I am better than him,” Iblis said. “You made me from fire, and him from clay.”

steps.q: What is wrong with Iblis’s argument?
o: He judged by what Adam was made of
He was right, but said it too proudly
He misunderstood the command to bow
steps.why: Clay, fire: he ranked the stuff, and left out what God put into Adam, His breath (15:29) and the names He taught him (2:31).

steps.q: The Arabic word for pride, kibr, shares a root with a phrase Muslims say many times a day. Which?
o: Bismillah, in the name of God
steps.why: K-b-r means greatness. Pride claims a greatness that belongs to God alone; “Allahu akbar” puts it back where it belongs.

steps.line: What held him back wasn’t hunger or fear. It was a comparison. Pride, the first wrong in the story.
The Prophet ﷺ defined pride simply: rejecting the truth, and looking down on people.

steps.q: The angels bowed to Adam, yet in Islam worship is for God alone. How do Muslims understand that bow?
o: A bow of honor, not worship
steps.why: Most scholars call it a bow of greeting and honor, made because God commanded it. Worship belongs to God alone.

steps.line: Today, someone younger is made team lead. A quiet thought arrives fully formed: under them? I’m better than that. It’s a very old thought.
steps.label: today

say: here’s what i love. the story’s first mistake isn’t violence. it’s a single thought: i’m better than him.
in islam, the angels’ bow honored adam; it wasn’t worship. and pride isn’t nice clothes, the prophet ﷺ said. God is beautiful and loves beauty. pride is looking down on people.

steps.q: Iblis claimed to be better because of what he was made of. From this lesson, what really counts in God’s eyes?
o: What you do with what you’re given
What you’re made of, or born into
How high you rise among others
steps.why: The Qur’an says the noblest in God’s sight are the most mindful of Him (49:13), not the best born. Iblis bet everything on his material.

today.say: today, catch one “i’m better than that” thought: in traffic, at work, scrolling. don’t argue with it. just name it, and let one person go ahead of you without minding. a saying teaches that whoever humbles themselves for God, God raises them.
options: lovely. naming it takes the fire out.
good. that’s the bow, in modern clothes.

tomorrow.line: a garden full of yeses, and a single no.

sources: Qur’an 7:11-12 (“He said: What hindered thee that thou didst not fall prostrate when I bade thee? (Iblis) said: I am better than him. Thou createdst me of fire while him Thou didst create of mud,” Pickthall)
Qur’an 2:34 (the angels fell prostrate, all save Iblis)
Qur’an 18:50 (Iblis “was of the jinn”); Qur’an 55:15 (the jinn created of smokeless fire)
Sahih Muslim 2588 (no one humbles himself for Allah but Allah raises him)
Qur’an 15:29 (God breathed into Adam of His spirit)

Sahih Muslim 91 (no one with an atom’s weight of pride in his heart will enter paradise; a man loves fine clothes and shoes; “Allah is beautiful and loves beauty. Pride is rejecting the truth and looking down on people”)
check: Whether Iblis was an angel or a jinn is discussed by commentators; the lesson follows 18:50. Confirm.
